 ----
 Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay

For the Petitioners : Mr. Kaushik Sarkhel, Advocate
 : Mr. Nitin Kumar Pasari, Advocate

For the State : Mr. K.K. Mishra, APP  -----
02/30.11.2017 It has been submitted by Mr. Kaushik Sarkhel, learned counsel for the petitioners, that edible oils,
which were allegedly seized, were not adulterated as test report suggests that the same were misbranded.
It has further been submitted that without awaiting for test report, FIR has been instituted against the petitioners.
It has also been submitted that steps were taken by the District Administration for cancellation of licence, which has been stayed by this Court in W.P.(C) No. 5965 of 2017.
Learned counsel submits that a show cause notice was also issued to the petitioner no. 3 as to why the licence should not be cancelled, which has already been stayed by this Court.

Learned counsel further submits that in view of Section 89 of the Food Safety and Standard Act,
2008, it can be said to have an overriding effect of this Act over all other food related laws.

Learned counsel thus submits that entire criminal proceeding as against the petitioners deserves to Kamal Chhaparia And Ors vs The State Of Jharkhand And Anr on 30 November, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19883512/
1 be quashed and set aside in view of the aforesaid facts.

sentences.text: Mr. K.K. Mishra, learned A.P.P., undertakes to appear on behalf of O.P. No. 2.
He is directed to file a counter affidavit, for which he is granted six weeks' time.
List this case after six weeks under the heading "For Admission".

Until further orders, there shall be no coercive steps against the petitioners in connection with Kotwali P.S. Case No. 129 of 2017, G.R. No. 2807 of 2017, pending in the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi.
Let a copy of the order be given to learned A.P.P. and his name be also reflected in the cause list.
(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J) Rakesh/
